content.text:
## Findings

I ran 8 cold app-starts (kill + relaunch, no data clear) on the real device, navigating Home → About → Diagnostics each time and capturing the screen:

| # | Clock | Sync status shown | "Retry sync" button |
|---|-------|-------------------|---------------------|
| 1 | 8:11 | Sync idle | present |
| 2 | 8:11 | Sync idle (re-checked after tapping the button, same launch) | present, no change |
| 3 | 8:12 | **Sync unavailable** | absent |
| 4 | 8:12 | Sync idle | present |
| 5 | 8:12 | **Sync unavailable** | absent |
| 6 | 8:13 | Sync idle | present |
| 7 | 8:13 | Sync idle | present |
| 8 | 8:14 | **Sync unavailable** | absent |

(7 independent cold launches: 4 "idle" / 3 "unavailable" — a ~57% pass rate, matching the reported "passes about 3 times out of 5.")

**What the button depends on:** The Diagnostics screen renders a "Sync status" card whose body text is either "Sync idle" or "Sync unavailable." The "Retry sync" button is only emitted into the view hierarchy when the status is "Sync idle" — when it's "Sync unavailable," the button node doesn't exist at all (not just hidden/disabled), so any assertVisible on it fails outright.

**Why it flakes, ruled-out causes:**
- Not a loading race: after landing on "Sync unavailable," I waited 3s and re-captured — it never transitioned to idle, so it isn't a matter of the test asserting too early.
- Not tied to real connectivity: the status-bar Wi‑Fi ("Wifi signal full") and mobile signal ("AT&T, four bars") indicators were identical across every run, idle or unavailable.
- Not tied to wall-clock time/minute parity: idle and unavailable both occurred within the same minute (8:12) on different launches.
- Not persisted app state: launches used `stopApp` + `launchApp` without `clearState`, yet the outcome still flipped between consecutive cold starts — so it isn't read from a stored preference/DB value from a prior run either.

**Conclusion:** The sync-availability flag is decided freshly and effectively at random each time the app process starts (consistent with something like a `Random()`/timestamp-seeded coin-flip in the Diagnostics/sync init code), independent of network, time, or persisted state. Since "Retry sync" is conditionally composed only in the "idle" branch, the test is flaky because it's asserting on a UI element whose existence depends on this per-launch random outcome rather than on any deterministic app condition. Fix would be either to make the underlying "sync availability" simulation deterministic for tests (e.g., inject/mock it in test builds) or have the test explicitly handle/assert both states rather than assuming the button always exists.
